newsitem.title: IRAQ: U.N. ENVOY IN IRAQ TO REVIEW OIL-FOR-FOOD SNAGS.
newsitem.headline: U.N. ENVOY IN IRAQ TO REVIEW OIL-FOR-FOOD SNAGS.

text.p: U.N. Under-Secretary General Yasushi Akashi arrived in Baghdad on Saturday to review problems in the implementation of Iraq's oil-for-food deal.

The deal went into effect in December, and allows Iraq to sell $2 billion worth of oil over six months to buy food, medicine and other humanitarian supplies, as an exception to the sanctions imposed on Baghdad by the U.N. after its 1990 invasion of Kuwait.
"There are still some problems...You have to be patient. We are determined to acquire even greater speed," Akashi told reporters on arrival.

"The United Nations wants to expedite the importation and distribution of these goods so that they can be distributed on a fair and equitable basis to all the civilian population in need," Akashi said.
Akashi said implementation was being delayed by what he called "difficulties of political, bureaucrtatic, operational and technical nature."
He said however, U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan attached high priority to the deal and the problems were being gradually resolved.

Iraq has complained about sluggish approval of contracts for the purchase of humanitarian goods. The government says no medical supplies have arrived and so far only wheat flour had been distributed to Iraqis.
Akashi said the U.N. had taken steps to accelerate implementation, including the recruitment of more experts to examine contracts, especially those related to medical supplies.
Akashi said part of his mission would be to express U.N. concerns to the Iraqis and convey back whatever concerns Iraq might have about the deal. The programme expires on June 7.
The U.N. Secretary-General is to submit a report before then to the Security Council, which must decide whether the programme should be extended.
Akashi is expected to spend six days in Iraq. Apart from meetings with Iraqi officials, he will visit Iraq's three Kurdish provinces in the north.
